notes: Hashes are md5 over the RAW pixel buffer (Image.GetData()), never over the saved PNG.
A GPU or driver change legitimately moves every hash at once; the gpu field above is what these were captured on. Regenerate after a driver update, and say so in the commit message.
A landed visual change updates this file in the SAME commit and names the shots it moved. An unexplained flip is a stop-the-line finding, not a regeneration.
The runner appends --screenshot=<abs path> and --log-file=<abs path>; everything else is the args below verbatim.

shots.name: c1-waterfall
shots.exercises: UV scroll on the falls sheet + the mist puffer; frame-sensitive 1.28 % at 120 vs 121.

shots.name: c1b-night-sea
shots.exercises: night lighting, skydome, islands, the ambient cloud-puff field; static at 120 vs 121, 0.13 % at 120 vs 360 (puff drift).

shots.name: c1c-rain
shots.exercises: rain precipitation (seeded field on the sim clock), cloud deck, heavy fog; frame-sensitive 2.50 %.

shots.name: c2-city
shots.exercises: C2's solid 3D city blocks, billboard clutter, backlot geometry, daylight fog; near-static, 51 px at 120 vs 121.

shots.name: c2b-rain
shots.exercises: rain over open water — the surface A3 measured at 4.75 % unpinned; frame-sensitive 3.47 %.

shots.name: c3-island
shots.exercises: coastline, surf edge and open water at close range; static — 9 px at 120 vs 360, so it proves geometry and shading, not the clock.

shots.name: c4-snow
shots.exercises: snow precipitation plus the chapter carrying 6 UV-scroll models; frame-sensitive 3.74 %, the largest of the freecam set.

shots.name: c5-city-night
shots.exercises: the night city: LIGHT_STATE point lights packed into csky_light_data, lit window skins, moon and stars; static, 11 px at 120 vs 360.

shots.name: viewer-bhawk
shots.exercises: one aircraft built and painted: PlaneBuilder, the pinned livery seed, decals, the orbit camera's framing; static by construction, 0 px at 30 vs 360.

shots.name: empty-stage
shots.exercises: the synthetic stage with no gamez at all — code-drawn grid, default sky and sun, flight model, HUD; frame-sensitive 12.21 %, and the one shot that still renders with extracted/ absent.

shots.name: c1-flight
shots.exercises: a flying plane: chase camera on the sim clock, prop and control-surface animators, gauges, compass tape, weapon readout, impact reticle; the --hold throttle 0.5→1 jump also crosses ThrottleSlamSmoke's slam threshold, so this is the one golden carrying a live exhaust-trail Puffer; frame-sensitive 34.52 %, the strongest tripwire here.

shots.name: c1-destroy-effects
shots.exercises: the world-effects runtime (ForEffects/D32) built and rendering a puffer: a flight-session kill of the single ap_radiotwr instance CALL_ANIMATIONs great_balls_of_fire onto the world-effects stage; frame-sensitive (distinct hashes at 119/120/121), and moves off its Rng.Effects seed (PLAN-animruntime-role-factories A1).

shots.name: c1-crash
shots.exercises: the per-player crash rig (ForCrashRig/D32) constructing and playing player_crash_dirt: --crash=5 forces FlightController.Crash() at a fixed sim frame, the only headless trigger for this path (PLAN-animruntime-role-factories A2); moves off its Rng.Crash draw. The set's biggest puffer surface, so the TEXTURE_SEQUENCE lifetime-fraction fix moved 26.55 % of its pixels: the fireball holds its mid flipbook frames instead of the blown-out last one. Also exercises EffectCatalogue.CrashSurfaceLevelAnimNames (BL-292): flydirt_plane, the dirt burst's ground-scorch dust plane, levels to world axes instead of the plane's spawn-trim attitude at --crash=5's frame, moving a 2.16% halo ring around the fireball (>20/255 threshold) — the fireball/smoke/debris family is deliberately excluded from that set and is pixel-unchanged.
